findings.description: Domain-model mismatch on what "tax-adjusted figures" means. The real Tax tab (`render_tax`, TAX_HEADER = Sale ID/Lot ID/Jurisdiction/Tax Year/Amount/Lifecycle State, plus TAX_RESERVE_HEADER = Jurisdiction/Tax Year/Accrued/Moved/Paid/Outstanding/Shortfall) contains ZERO cost-basis/proceeds/gain figures — it is a tax reserve-liability accrual ledger, not a P&L-adjusted-for-tax view. The actual 'adjusted for tax' P&L computation (Est. Unrealized Tax, Net Unrealized, fed by tax::effective_rate) lives on the POSITIONS tab via live formulas (=G*H, =G*(1-H)) — the very tab SHEET-FORMULA-004 says the Tax tab must be 'distinct from.' All three A drafts, reading 'tax-adjusted figures' cold, independently built cost-basis/proceeds/gain data models for the Tax tab (A1: short_term_adj/long_term_adj/total_adj; A2 & A3: cost_basis_cents/proceeds_cents/realized_gain_cents/unrealized_gain_cents per lot) — none of which exist in real render_tax. B1 independently catches the exact same tension in its scope note: 'The Tax tab itself (render_tax) carries NO tax-*adjusted* computed figures... The only tax-adjusted *estimate* computation in these files is on the Positions tab.' Both directions converge on the same gap from opposite sides.

"As-of-last-sync" is asserted in prose but not operative in code. `pub fn render_tax(accruals: &[Accrual], annual_rows: &[AnnualRow]) -> TaxView` takes no timestamp/sync argument, and neither `TaxView` nor any Tax-tab test (formula.rs, tabs.rs) carries or asserts a last-sync marker anywhere — the phrase 'kernel-exact, stacked, as-of-last-sync' exists only as doc-comment rationale on render_tax (line ~695), never as a field, cell, or test assertion. Forced by the explicit spec phrase, all three A drafts invented a timestamp mechanism with no code counterpart: A1 uses per-row `Option<DateTime<Utc>>` with snapshot fallback and a 'not yet synced' render path; A2 uses a mandatory snapshot-level `DateTime<Utc>`; A3 surfaces `as_of_sync` in a banner row. On the B side, all three reconstructions can only echo the doc-comment rationale phrase without citing any operative field or test enforcing it, because none exists — the code side independently confirms the qualifier is unenforced.

Extensive code-side structural surplus the one-sentence EARS text never states, reconstructed near-verbatim across B1/B2/B3: (a) the Tax tab is physically TWO separate named/typed ranges (TAX_TAB accrual band vs TAX_RESERVE_TAB reserve-summary band) at different aggregation grains (one row per Accrual vs one row per (Jurisdiction, TaxYear) AnnualRow) — none of the three A drafts anticipated a two-band split, each built one unified row/lot set instead; (b) the exact header column lists; (c) the fmt_cents rule (`{sign}{whole}.{frac:02}`, e.g. Cents(-5) -> "-0.05"); (d) Jurisdiction rendering ("Federal" / "State({code})"); (e) Lifecycle State rendered as bare variant name only, discarding Allocated{..}/Moved{..}/Paid{..} payload data; (f) Amount renders empty string when applied_cents is None vs fmt_cents when Some; (g) all five reserve-summary columns are never blank even at zero (pinned by reserve_summary_carries_all_five_kernel_exact_columns); (h) a dedicated 'no among-data row' invariant — no blank/separator/'RESERVE SUMMARY'-label row, no embedded second header inside the accrual band — enforced by tax_accrual_band_has_no_among_data_summary_rows and assertions in publishes_four_view_tabs_one_row_per_entity. None of this is derivable from 'kernel-exact (stacked, as-of-last-sync) tax-adjusted figures, distinct from the Positions live estimate.'

The single word "stacked" is left fully open by the spec text and none of the three A drafts converge with each other, let alone with the code: A1 reads it as short-term/long-term tax-adjustment layers summed to a total; A2 and A3 read it as one row per tax lot (with a long/short-term boolean/enum). The real code's actual 'stacked' structure (per its own doc comments) is the two-band accrual+reserve-summary split described in finding 3 — a reading none of the three A drafts produced. This is a secondary symptom of the same ambiguity as findings 1 and 3 rather than an independent gap, but it shows the spec's parenthetical qualifier is not just under-specified but actively mis-cues fresh implementers toward a per-lot/per-symbol gain-layering model that has no code counterpart.

notes:
A-side agreement is strong on the outer shell (Cents as i64, kernel-exact = literal Value never Formula/GOOGLEFINANCE, sheets-view performs zero accounting/tax math, distinctness from Positions implemented structurally) but diverges meaningfully on two sub-decisions the spec leaves open: (1) what \"stacked\" groups by — A1 (ST/LT layers -> total) vs A2/A3 (per-lot rows) — and (2) how \"as-of-last-sync\" is modeled — A1 uses Option<DateTime> with a \"not yet synced\" fallback state, while A2 and A3 explicitly reject Option and assume the kernel always supplies a timestamp. None of the three A drafts anticipated the real two-band (accrual + reserve-summary) architecture or the reserve/liability (Accrued/Moved/Paid/Outstanding/Shortfall) domain — all three instead modeled a cost-basis/gain-adjustment domain that doesn't exist on the real Tax tab.

B-side agreement is very tight: B1, B2, and B3 independently reconstruct the same two-band architecture, the same header lists, the same fmt_cents formatting rule, the same Jurisdiction/Lifecycle-State rendering conventions, and the same null/never-blank handling, differing only in that B1 additionally scopes out to the Positions tab's actual tax-adjusted (post-tax estimate) formulas with an explicit scope note explaining why — a difference in coverage/thoroughness, not disagreement.

Overall: this spec (SHEET-FORMULA-004) is a single dense sentence trying to cover a two-band, multi-invariant, cross-tab-boundary feature; the audit finds real, concrete, well-corroborated bidirectional drift rather than noise from either side.
